I've been growing cotton on this land my whole life — 46 years. I know this soil, I know when the rains come late, I know how the bollworms move in July. My land is 10.9 mu and I plant all of it in cotton. That's what this county does. That's what I do.

At my age, me and my household member can still manage 10.9 mu but I can't take risks. I plant hybrid seed — I switched years ago because the yields are better and I've seen what happens when neighbors try to save their own seed. Not worth it.

For fertilizer, I put down a base dressing before planting — urea and phosphate, the way I've always mixed it. I top dress twice during the growing season, before flowering and when bolls are setting. I don't have a measuring scale, I go by the bag counts I've done for years — it works out to roughly 18 jin of nitrogen fertilizer per mu, less phosphorus, a bit of potash. My well gives me water when heaven doesn't. I irrigate four times — once before sowing to wet the bed, once at seedling stage, once heavy during boll development in July, once more in August if the heat holds. Cotton draws pests badly. I spray five times — I start watching for aphids in June and don't stop until September. I plough every year before planting. Rotary isn't deep enough for cotton roots on my plot.

I expect around 250 jin of seed cotton per mu. Some years more, some less.
